newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC INTO SEMIS AFTER KORDA PULLS OUT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC INTO SEMIS AFTER KORDA PULLS OUT.

text.p: Top seed Goran Ivanisevic reached the semifinals of the world indoor tournament on Friday without hitting a ball when opponent Petr Korda pulled out with a back injury.
The 25-year-old titleholder received a walkover after Czech eighth seed Korda pulled out after suffering the injury while training on Thursday.
"It is an injury to his lower back. He can't bend over," tournament director Wim Buitendijk said.
Ivanisevic, who has successfully defended two titles this year, will meet Korda's compatriot Daniel Vacek, who beat Italian Renzo Furlan 6-4 1-6 6-3.

Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek, seeded second, beat Michael Stich of Germany 7-6 7-6 and will meet third-seeded Swede Thomas Enqvist in Saturday's other semifinal. Enqvist defeated Germany's Alex Radulescu 7-6 6-3.

Krajicek, returning to form after a knee operation at the end of last year, served 18 aces but was broken in the fourth game of the first set. He broke back in the seventh to take the set to a tie-break, which he won 7-4.
In the second set both Krajicek, winner here in 1995, and Stich, who won the tournament in 1994, held serve before the Dutch player took the tie-break 7-3.
"It was by far the best match this year. Earlier in the week the form was not yet there, but now I am a candidate to win the title here," said Krajicek.
